sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Ni–Ti binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset NiTi-04Tok.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → (Ni) + Ni3Ti, lies at 1575.6 K.
The Ni–Ti system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as intermetallic rich, congruent compound.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry (Hallstedt, 2025), which reproduces the assessment of T. Tokunaga, K. Hashima, H. Ohtani, M. Hasebe, Mater. Trans. JIM, 45, 1507-14(2004).
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Ni reproduced by the dataset is 1728.2 K.
For Ti, the liquidus meets the axis at 2498.8 K.
The dataset places a eutectic (L → (Ni) + Ni3Ti) at 1575.6 K; the composition of L is 16.6 at.% Ti.
The eutectic reaction L → Ni3Ti + NiTi is calculated at 1393.0 K, with L at 38.4 at.%.
We obtain 1259.5 K for the peritectic reaction (NiTi + L → NiTi2), where L has 66.9 at.% Ti.
We obtain 1216.3 K for the eutectic reaction (L → NiTi2 + (βTi)), where L has 74.6 at.% Ti.
We obtain 1040.8 K for the eutectoid reaction ((βTi) → NiTi2 + (αTi)), where (βTi) has 94.7 at.%.
Ni3Ti melts congruently at 1649.4 K and 23.7 at.% Ti.
NiTi2 melts congruently at 1259.5 K and 66.7 at.% Ti.
At 2600 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −40.84 kJ/mol, at 38.0 at.% Ti.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of NiTi2 at 298.15 K is −26.90 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
